output.headline: Pays School Facility Consultants up to $190,000 to help win state school construction funding
output.summary: School Facility Consultants will help the district work out and claim state funding eligibility for new school construction, modernization and joint-use projects. That includes preparing applications to the California Department of Education and the State Allocation Board. The contract is capped at $190,000 for July 1, 2021 through June 30, 2022.

output.headline: Extends Dialog Design's Madison Park Academy expansion contract by a year, with no added money
output.summary: This amendment gives Dialog Design, LP (also known as Byrens Kim Design Works) 365 more days on its architectural services agreement for the Madison Park Academy Expansion Project. The end date moves from December 31, 2020 to December 30, 2021. The original agreement dates back to March 12, 2014. No money is added, and part of the added period came before this vote.

vendor.name: Dialog Design, LP (aka Byrens Kim Design Works)

output.headline: Awards Data Media Services $62,000 to install 25 security cameras at Oakland Tech and Melrose sites
output.summary: Data Media Services, the lowest responsive bidder in a competitive bid, will install 25 exterior cameras and program the servers and software for the Video Surveillance Project. Sites include Oakland Technical High School and two Melrose Leadership Academy campuses. The $62,000 includes a $6,000 contingency. Work is expected to run 90 days, from August 12 to November 10, 2021.

output.headline: Pays Consolidated Engineering Laboratories up to $36,367 for testing at Lincoln Elementary repairs

money.evidence: total not to exceed amount of $36,367.00

output.sourceIssueCandidate: The text calls the $10,000 contingency a 10% fee, but $10,000 is about 38% of the $26,367 base amount.
output.summary: Consolidated Engineering Laboratories will provide materials testing and construction inspection for the water intrusion repairs at Lincoln Elementary School. The price is $26,367 for basic services plus $10,000 held for additional services if needed, for a cap of $36,367. Work was scheduled to start June 16, 2021, before this vote, and to run through August 23, 2021, though it may last longer if delays arise.

output.headline: Pays Xebec Data Corporation up to $4,000 to set up energy data exchange with PG&E
output.summary: Xebec Data Corporation will set up and test an online data-exchange system so the district can send and receive energy-use data with PG&E, the utility, for the Prop 39 energy operations project. The agreement is capped at $4,000 and runs July 1, 2021 through June 30, 2022.

output.headline: Approves the district's 2021-22 funding application to the state through the CARS system
output.summary: The board approves the district's 2021-2022 application for funding through the state's Consolidated Application and Reporting System (CARS). It also authorizes the Superintendent, or a designee, to submit the application to the California Department of Education. No dollar amount is stated.

output.headline: Approves the 2021-22 summary of how Proposition 30 Education Protection Account funds will be spent
output.summary: The board approves a resolution summarizing how the district will spend its Education Protection Account money (state funds from Proposition 30) in the 2021-22 fiscal year. The official text does not state a dollar amount.

output.headline: Allows temporary borrowing between district funds in 2021-22 to cover cash-flow needs
output.summary: The board approves a resolution that lets the district borrow temporarily from one of its funds to another during the 2021-22 fiscal year when cash is short, and sets how the borrowed money is repaid. It cites Education Code Section 42603. No dollar amount is stated.

output.headline: Shares student data at no cost with Oakland Public Education Fund, Oakland REACH and two others
output.summary: The district will share student-level data with The Oakland Public Education Fund, The Oakland REACH, CARES for Learning, and The New Teacher Project (TNTP). The groups will use it to understand students' earlier reading performance, track literacy growth and school engagement, keep families informed, and support families. The agreement covers April 21, 2021 to June 30, 2022 and costs the district nothing.

output.headline: Renews Brandman University partnership for teacher, counselor and psychologist interns through 2024
output.summary: The district and Brandman University, a private nonprofit university, renew an agreement for intern and practicum placements. It covers K-12 teaching, education specialist, school counselor, clinical school psychologist and administrative services credentials, plus other student support credentials. It runs from July 1, 2021 to June 30, 2024. The text does not state a dollar amount.

output.headline: Accepts a $5,000 Project Lead The Way grant for the engineering program at Oakland High
output.summary: Project Lead the Way, Inc. is giving the district $5,000 to offset the costs of its Project Lead the Way Engineering Program at Oakland High School. The grant period runs from February 25, 2021 to May 31, 2022, so it began before this vote.

output.headline: Accepts a $5,000 Project Lead The Way grant for the engineering program at McClymonds High
output.summary: Project Lead the Way, Inc. is giving the district $5,000 to offset the costs of its Project Lead the Way Engineering Program at McClymonds High School. The grant period runs from February 25, 2021 to May 31, 2022, so it began before this vote.

output.headline: Accepts a $5,000 Project Lead The Way grant for the engineering program at Madison Park Academy
output.summary: Project Lead the Way, Inc. is giving the district $5,000 to offset the costs of its Project Lead the Way Engineering Program at Madison Park Academy 6-12. The grant period runs from February 25, 2021 to May 31, 2022, so it began before this vote.

output.headline: Accepts a $5,000 Project Lead The Way grant for the Gateway program at West Oakland Middle
output.summary: Project Lead the Way, Inc. is giving the district $5,000 to offset the costs of its Project Lead the Way Gateway Program at West Oakland Middle School. The grant period runs from February 25, 2021 to May 31, 2022, so it began before this vote.

output.headline: Accepts a $10,000 Project Lead The Way grant for the Launch program at International Community School
output.summary: Project Lead the Way, Inc. is giving the district $10,000 to offset the costs of its Project Lead the Way Launch Program at International Community School. The grant period runs from February 25, 2021 to May 31, 2023, so it began before this vote.

output.headline: Accepts a $5,000 Project Lead The Way grant for the Launch program at Hoover Elementary
output.summary: Project Lead the Way, Inc. is giving the district $5,000 to offset the costs of its Project Lead the Way Launch Program at Hoover Elementary School. The grant period runs from February 25, 2021 to May 31, 2022, so it began before this vote.

output.headline: Adds $18,500 for Be The Change Consulting to run George Floyd Safety Plan design meetings
output.summary: The board ratifies, meaning approves after the fact, a change that raises the contract with Be The Change Consulting from $30,000 to $48,500, an added $18,500. The firm facilitates process design team meetings for the George Floyd Safety Plan. The amendment covers April 1 to June 30, 2021, which was already over before this vote.

output.headline: Buys up to $2M in food from Sysco for student meals through Dec. 2021 without a public bid

money.evidence: in an amount not to exceed $2,000,000.00

output.summary: The district is hiring Sysco San Francisco to supply extra meat, poultry, high-protein foods and fresh produce for its student meal program from August 12 to December 31, 2021. The district is skipping its own public bidding by using a legal exception to public bidding (called the Graydon exception). The contract is capped at $2,000,000.

output.headline: Updates the independent study policy (BP 6158) to match the new state law AB 130
output.summary: The board adopts a resolution amending Board Policy 6158 on independent study (learning outside the regular classroom) so it lines up with AB 130, a state law enacted July 9, 2021. No dollar amount is stated.

output.headline: Asks Alameda County to set the tax rate for school bonds expected to be sold in 2021-22
output.summary: The board adopts a resolution asking the Alameda County Board of Supervisors to set the property tax rate for Oakland Unified bonds that are expected to be sold during the 2021-22 fiscal year. It also authorizes the actions needed to carry this out. No dollar amount is stated.
